item.title: Bitget UEX Daily | Nasdaq Slumps as Nvidia Probe Adds to AI Selloff; Bitcoin Reclaims $60,000 Over the Weekend (November 23, 2026)

item.content:encoded: I. Hot News Highlights AI and Regulation: Nvidia Accounting Probe Adds Uncertainty On November 20, Reuters reported, citing sources, that the SEC was examining Nvidia’s accounting. The specific issues remain undisclosed, and the investigation has not established wrongdoing. US Economy: Consumer Sentiment Improves as Inflation Expectations Ease The University of Michigan’s final November sentiment index rose to 51.5 from 48.0 in October. One-year inflation expectations fell from 4.7% to 3.7%, while longer-term expectations declined from 3.5% to 3.3%; sentiment nevertheless remains weak, with inflation a leading concern. Resilient demand and easing price expectations can coexist. Actual spending and PCE data must now test that combination; the survey alone does not establish that interest-rate pressure has cleared. Weekend Policy: Chinese Exchanges Ease Margin Requirements On November 22, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges announced that the minimum financing margin ratio would fall from 100% to 80% on November 30. Shanghai and Shenzhen also announced fee reductions, with Monday’s turnover and market response providing an initial test of their impact. II. Market Review Market Moves Explained Market performance: The Nasdaq fell 5.28% on Friday, the S&P 500 lost 3.70%, and the Dow dropped 1.93%, with all seven megacaps lower. Nvidia fell 14.01%, AMD and Micron each lost more than 13%, while CoreWeave and Nebius declined 12.02% and 16.11%; bitcoin touched roughly $55,252 over the weekend before reclaiming $60,000. First, investors are questioning who ultimately funds AI spending. Strong chip sales demonstrate infrastructure demand, but do not establish that cloud providers and model companies have earned adequate returns. If end-user revenue fails to cover compute, power and financing costs, expansion becomes more dependent on continued access to capital. Second, high rates pressure both valuations and project economics. Companies with distant profits and substantial funding needs face higher financing costs and lower present values for future cash flow. The sharper declines in neocloud stocks are consistent with investors differentiating funding capacity and cash-flow quality. Third, risks at a market leader spread through crowded positions. Nvidia’s decline weakened a key valuation anchor for chips, cloud infrastructure and related equipment. Treasury yields fell on Friday without arresting the technology selloff, suggesting that exposure reduction also mattered beyond the day’s rate move. Commodities and Foreign Exchange Asset Reference level Basis Spot gold $3,520.09/oz Friday, late New York session Spot silver $40.95/oz Friday, late New York session WTI crude $83.41/bbl January 2027 contract, Friday closing reference Brent crude $92.57/bbl January 2027 contract, Friday settlement US Dollar Index 103.81 Friday closing reference US 10-year Treasury yield 4.912% Friday closing reference Precious metals weakened alongside risk assets, while Treasuries attracted some support. Oil recovered on Friday, and the weekend attack on an industrial facility in Bahrain kept supply risks in focus alongside demand concerns. Cryptocurrency Performance BTC traded at 60,940.92 USDT, up 1.05% over 24 hours; ETH stood at 1,712.92 USDT, up 1.35%. Total crypto market capitalization was approximately $2.11 trillion, down 2.18%, with 24-hour volume of $62.53 billion; aggregate data were updated at 22:55 Beijing time on November 22. BTC | Liquidation Zones: A conspicuous potential short-liquidation cluster lies around $61,400–$62,300, approximately 0.86%–2.34% above the current price; the lower potential long-liquidation cluster is around $60,000–$60,600, approximately 0.45%–1.43% below. The lower zone is closer, making a retreat into it relevant for potential liquidation-driven volatility. ETH | Liquidation Zones: A conspicuous potential short-liquidation cluster lies around $1,720–$1,740, approximately 0.52%–1.69% above the current price; the lower potential long-liquidation cluster is around $1,675–$1,695, approximately 0.94%–2.11% below. The upper zone is closer, where short liquidations could accelerate a rebound. Institutional Cost Basis | BTC: Strategy disclosed on November 16 that it held 850,849 BTC as of November 15, at an average acquisition cost of approximately $75,452 including fees. Bitcoin is about 19.32% below that cost; this is a price-to-acquisition-cost comparison, not the company’s overall financial return. Market Takeaway: Watch BTC buying interest around $60,000–$60,600 and follow-through above $61,400, alongside ETH’s response around $1,720–$1,740. Monday’s equities and ETF flows will help assess whether the weekend recovery can extend. Major US Indices Index Close Daily change Dow Jones 48,147.33 -1.93% S&P 500 6,910.39 -3.70% Nasdaq Composite 22,617.73 -5.28% The S&P 500 and Dow are both more than 10% below their record closing highs, meeting the usual definition of a correction. The S&P’s seventh consecutive decline shows that pressure extends beyond one company. Magnificent Seven Company Close (USD) Daily change Nvidia (NVDA) 125.53 -14.01% Apple (AAPL) 342.56 -1.90% Microsoft (MSFT) 484.52 -2.77% Alphabet (GOOGL) 265.29 -2.70% Amazon (AMZN) 246.82 -4.10% Meta (META) 560.84 -5.93% Tesla (TSLA) 345.82 -7.64% All seven fell, led by Nvidia and Tesla, while Apple was relatively resilient. Watch whether selling spreads further into steadier cash-flow businesses and whether any leader-led rebound broadens across the sector. Sector Moves Semiconductors and cloud infrastructure: AMD lost 13.25% and Micron declined 13.89%, alongside sharp neocloud losses. Distinguish actual orders and project financing from any subsequent stock-price recovery. Crypto-linked equities: Strategy fell 9.67%, Coinbase lost 6.34%, and Robinhood declined 9.44% at Friday’s close. Whether the weekend crypto rebound carries into these stocks remains a question for Monday’s opening. Stock-specific resilience: UnitedHealth gained 2.84%, alongside a TD Cowen upgrade from Hold to Buy. Individual catalysts still produced gains, but one stock does not establish a sector-wide reversal. III. In-Depth US Equity Analysis Nvidia (NVDA): Strong Earnings Meet a Higher Risk Discount Event overview: Shares closed at $125.53 on Friday, down 14.01%. Previously reported quarterly revenue reached $115.8 billion, up 103%, with next-quarter revenue guidance of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. Market interpretation: Strong realized sales have not stabilized the stock. Customer funding, cash collection and project returns also affect the valuation investors will accept. Investment implications: Next-quarter gross-margin guidance of 71%–72% is below the roughly 75% reported last quarter. Watch product-ramp margins, receivables, cash flow and formal regulatory disclosures. Anthropic (ANT): IPO Premium Narrows as Execution Takes Focus Event overview: Shares fell 8.50% to $88.91 on Friday, remaining 7.12% above the $83 offering price. The second-day decline showed that IPO enthusiasm offered limited insulation from the AI selloff. Market interpretation: Model capability and commercial returns require separate assessment. Revenue growth needs to be evaluated alongside compute purchases, customer retention and cash consumption. Investment implications: The $83 offering price is a reference, not assured support. Enterprise monetization, unit compute costs and cash consumption will help assess whether growth improves operating cash flow. Intuit (INTU): Revised Growth Outlook Meets a Planned Divestiture Event overview: Shares fell 12.77% to $270.44 on Friday. Quarterly revenue rose 12% to $4.4 billion, and the company announced a planned $3.68 billion Mailchimp sale. Market interpretation: Full-year revenue growth guidance moved to 8%–9%, while operating-income and EPS guidance were maintained. Investors must reassess the durability of both sales growth and margin improvement. Investment implications: Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to approvals and other conditions; current guidance excludes the sale’s effects. Watch Credit Karma, completion and updated guidance before treating planned buybacks as realized benefits. IV. Market & Project Updates BTC ETF outflows persist. Reported US spot BTC ETF flows for November 16–20 totaled approximately $1.245 billion in net withdrawals, including $124.5 million reported for Friday. IBIT’s Friday figure remains missing, making the weekly total incomplete; the weekend price rebound does not establish renewed ETF inflows. Chainflip discloses stolen assets and recovery terms. The project says the November 21 incident involved roughly 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH and 4.0078 million USDC and USDT combined, and offered a 10% bounty for returning 90%. Watch recovery and service-restoration progress; initial single-chain estimates are not the final total loss. Prediction-market legislation advances. The Senate passed the DEATH BETS Act, which would prohibit CFTC-regulated entities from listing or clearing contracts involving war, assassination, terrorism or individual deaths. Further legislative steps remain, including the House; it is not an enacted ban. COP31 ends without a final agreement. The EU and others rejected the final draft on November 22 amid disagreements over fossil fuels and climate finance. The outcome adds policy uncertainty, without directly establishing stronger near-term oil and gas demand. V. Today’s Market Calendar Beijing time Country/region Event Focus November 23, all day Japan Labor Thanksgiving Day closure; no derivatives holiday trading ★★ November 23, 21:30 US October Chicago Fed National Activity Index ★★ November 23, 22:45 US November flash manufacturing, services and composite PMIs; one release ★★★ November 23, 23:00 US Chicago Fed Survey of Economic Conditions ★★ November 24, 02:00 US Two-year Treasury auction ★★★ Event preview: PMI new orders and prices will help assess demand and cost pressures, while the Treasury auction tests short-end demand. PCE, GDP and spending data follow this week; US stocks close for Thanksgiving on November 26 and finish early on November 27, potentially amplifying moves around concentrated releases and thinner holiday trading. Institutional view: On November 20, Cetera CIO Gene Goldman distinguished the earnings test passed by chipmakers from the valuation test facing AI listings. That distinction frames the week: can operating results support the price investors pay for future growth? For market information only; not investment advice.
